rationale: Substantival relative formed on ϫⲁⲥⲉ/ϫⲓⲥⲉ 'be high, exalted.' Recurs three times on this page (lines 5, 11) as the heavenly archetype whose image is imprinted upon Adam-and-Eve. Translated 'the Exalted One' to preserve the active-verbal participial quality (per correspondential principle: a divine title from a verb of elevation should preserve the verb's elevated-action quality, not flatten to static 'High One').

Etymology uncertain. Possibly Lyc. variant of ⲟⲩⲱⲩ 'magnificent, noble' or related to ⲱⲩ 'great.' Context (parallel with ⲉⲗⲉⲩⲑⲉⲣⲁ 'free,' ⲉⲩⲅⲉⲛⲏⲥ 'noble,' ⲁⲝⲓⲱⲙⲁⲧⲓⲕⲏ 'titles of dignity') supports the noble/nobility reading. Confidence moderate.
= Coptic ⲥⲙⲟⲧ 'form, fashion, manner.' Already attested in glossary as ⲡⲓⲥⲛⲩ 'this manner.' On this page (line 12) used in 'the form of the tree' — the molded shape that is only a likeness.
Greek loanword κοιτών 'bed-chamber.' The lady's inner chamber from which she does not emerge — the hidden seat of her beauty in the parable. Recurs at line 21 and 28.
Latin palatium via Greek παλάτιον. The noblewoman's palace where she is hidden (line 24). Standard royal-residential term.
Greek ἀξιωματική. The dignified titles or ranks belonging to the noblewoman's status, paired with ⲉⲗⲉⲩⲑⲉⲣⲁ 'free habits' as the marks of her station.
Greek loanword ἕξις 'habit, condition, state of being.' Plural ϩⲛ̄ϩⲉⲝⲓⲥ 'habits' — the stable conditions in which the noblewoman exists. Standard philosophical-Greek term.

Possibly = Coptic ⲗⲓⲃⲉ 'be mad, rage' or ⲗⲱⲃⲉ 'long for, desire passionately.' Substantival qualitative 'the one longing.' Context (paired with ⲣ̄ⲉⲡⲓⲑⲩⲙⲏ 'desire' in next line) supports the longing/desiring sense.
Lycopolitan adverbial idiom: ⲣ̄- + ⲡⲧⲕⲉⲟ ('the additional thing' = ⲡϯⲕⲉⲟⲩⲁ). 'She does also/moreover.' Discourse-additive marker linking the lady's nobility to her beauty.

Coptic ⲥⲱⲛⲧ̄ 'create, fashion' substantivized = 'creation, that-which-is-created.' The 'inward heart of their creation' (line 2-3) is where the image of the Exalted One was imprinted upon the molded Adam and Eve.
